[[Category:Killycurragh Townland, Derryloran Parish, County Tyrone]]
== Biography ==
Jane was born about 1828.<ref>Given as age 22 on marriage 1850.</ref>
She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-1654|David Glasgow]]. 
<ref>Named on the marriage -- and she is definitely the sister of [[Glasgow-1653|Nancy Ann (Glasgow) Henry]] because Jane's husband James Ferguson is listed as brother-in-law on Nancy's husband's funeral.</ref>

On 3 Oct 1850 at Oritor Presbyterian, she married James Ferguson(23) of Killycurragh, son of Robert Ferguson, farmer. Witnessed by James Glasgow and William Ferguson.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/119f603202309 James Ferguson, Jane Glasgow, 31 Oct 1850, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref>

She passed away 24 Nov 1901 at Killycurragh age 72 due to influenza. Attended by Robert Ferguson , son, Killycurragh.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/7f75fb4523651 Jane Ferguson, 1901, Cookstown, 72] at Irish Civil Registration - Deaths</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1654]] is assessed at 94% (proved). Jane’s marriage-based father statement names David and ties the bride to Killycurragh and the Ferguson family. That directly supports a record-defined David father; the unresolved possibility of multiple Davids limits identification across the whole sibling group, not the parent clause.

Held citation and associated narrative supports this specific paternal assessment; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Compare the full 1850 father occupation and witnesses with other children’s marriages.

Source basis already held: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/119f603202309 James Ferguson, Jane Glasgow, 31 Oct 1850, Cookstown (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/119f603202309) at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
